title: Evaluation task
description: A task under evals/tasks/ (design v3 §10.2). Two properties make the numbers mean anything: the acceptance files are never in the worktree while the task runs, and the system's own verdict is recorded separately from the ground truth.

objective.description: What the system is asked to do, in the words a user would use. It must not name the fix: an objective that says what to change measures typing, not engineering.

fixture.description: Directory relative to the task file.

scope.description: Paths a solution may change, as a real task would restrict them.

leak_risk.description: Provenance is disclosed per task, never assumed. Results over public tasks are an upper bound and the report says so.

notes.description: What a reader of the results needs to interpret them: why the task is hard, and what a wrong-but-passing solution looks like.

max_wall_seconds.description: A result without a fixed budget is not comparable.

argv.description: Decides the task. A non-zero exit means it was not solved.

must_not_change.description: A task 'passed' by deleting the failing test has not been solved.

files.description: Written into the worktree copy AFTER the run. If the test is already in the fixture the model can read it, and satisfying a test you can see is not solving the problem.

set.description: Which evaluation set this task belongs to. Ranking weights, thresholds and retrieval constants may be fitted on dev; a held-out task is judged on and never fitted to, because a threshold chosen because it scored well on a task is no longer measured by that task. Absent means dev, which is the conservative reading.

origin.description: Where this task came from in real project history. It is the evidence the admission protocol checks: a task with no origin is one nobody can show is a real engineering problem rather than one written to be solvable. gold_revision is evaluator-only and must never be reachable from the fixture.

repository.description: The project, when the set draws on more than one.

base_revision.description: The pre-fix state the solver executes against.

gold_revision.description: The fixing commit. Evaluator-only: evidence for an annotator, never ground truth by itself.

base_digest.description: Content digest of the base state, from `bcode eval integrity --print-digest`. It is what makes the base revision checkable here: an edited fixture stops matching.

date.description: When the fix landed, for ordering a split by time and judging training-data leakage.

reference.description: A link or identifier a reader can follow.

derived_from_history.description: The objective was written from the real change rather than invented for the benchmark. A claim the author makes and a reviewer checks.

synthetic.description: Written for the benchmark. Allowed in dev, refused in a held-out publication set.

external_dependencies.description: Anything the acceptance check needs that is not in the fixture. A mandatory one makes the task unreproducible.

runtime_image.description: the immutable environment (name@sha256:…) this task's own verification runs in; empty means the host

runtime_workdir.description: where the worktree is mounted inside runtime_image

runtime_env.description: KEY=VALUE the runtime needs before the repository's checks will run

runtime_prepared_image.description: runtime_image with the repository's dependencies already fetched, so the measured run needs no network

runtime_prelude.description: a command run inside the runtime before each verification command, to restore what mounting the worktree displaced

traits.description: Facets the split protocol balances on and the duplicate audit groups by. Descriptive, not scored.

subsystem.description: The area of the project the work is in. Two tasks in one subsystem are the likeliest pair to leak across a split.

language.description: The primary language of the change.

family.description: Groups tasks a human judged to be variations of one problem. A declared family must not span dev and held-out.

expected.description: Localization ground truth, applied only when scoring and never shown to the system. Written by ApplyAnnotations from the annotation files rather than by hand: ground truth has provenance or it has no standing.
